title: Dynamo v1.6.0-beam-1.0-501b-dev.1
text:
Release Notes
Dynamo v1.6.0-beam-1.0-501b-dev.1 is an experimental snapshot build with early Reflection Beam-1.0-501B-A23B support on the Dynamo SGLang and vLLM backends. It is not recommended for production and is not a QA-gated release. APIs, behavior, and defaults may change before stable support. Use it for evaluation, testing, and early feedback only.
Summary
Dynamo v1.6.0-beam-1.0-501b-dev.1 serves reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B on Dynamo SGLang and vLLM. The frontend adds a Beam parser family on the unified v2 route and derives a Beam turn grammar for every chat turn, so tool calls, structured answers, and reasoning follow the model's channel format. /v1/completions can now echo the prompt with its logprobs. The vLLM runtime uses vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0-ubuntu2404 and the SGLang runtime uses lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130-runtime (#16702).
Kubernetes recipes cover aggregated and 1P1D disaggregated serving on both backends across H200, B200, B300, GB200, and GB300. Every target uses DFlash2 speculative decoding (block length 8), FP8 KV cache, KV-aware routing, and up to 1M tokens of context, with FP8 weights on H200 and NVFP4 weights on the Blackwell GPUs. The recipes include a shared model-cache PVC and download job, an AIPerf synthetic benchmark, and a recipe page on the docs site under recipes/beam-1.0-501b (#16666, #16677, cherry-picked in #16846).

About Beam-1.0-501B-A23B
Beam-1.0-501B-A23B is Reflection's Beam 1.0 model, published on Hugging Face as reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 and reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-FP8, with a reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2 draft checkpoint. This build serves it through Dynamo's SGLang and vLLM backends, aggregated or disaggregated, with DFlash2 speculative decoding and up to 1M tokens of context.
Full Changelog
Frontend (Beam Serving)
Beam parser family: Added the Beam parser family on the unified v2 route. The parser resumes in the channel an assistant prefill leaves open, and the Beam route keeps only the model's own stop-token text (#16702).
Beam turn grammar: Every chat turn is constrained by a structural-tag grammar derived from the Beam response template. Forced tool choices stay on the Harmony wire, builtin_tools are declared by name for the 1.0 chat template, and a response_format answer is held in the final channel with its tool arguments framed (#16702).
Request policy: Tools whose strict schema Beam cannot honor are served as non-strict, with one warning per request. preserve_thinking=false is accepted as a no-op, and allow_missing_thinking defaults to true (#16702).
Completions echo: /v1/completions echoes the prompt together with its logprobs (#16702).
Parser crates: Pinned dynamo-renderer 8.1.0 and dynamo-parsers-v2 0.10.0 from frontend-crates at the Beam release revision (ef8f4013, frontend-crates#430) (#16702).
vLLM Backend
Lazy engine-launch imports: The vLLM engine-launch imports load lazily, which the Beam vLLM engine needs, and chat_utils is imported from its new vLLM location when present (#16702).
Recipes
Beam-1.0-501B-A23B recipes: Added recipes/beam-1.0-501b with a shared model-cache PVC and download job, an AIPerf benchmark, and a docs-site recipe page (#16666, #16677, cherry-picked in #16846; recipe folder, recipe guide):
SGLang and vLLM, aggregated and 1P1D disaggregated, on H200 (FP8, 8 GPUs aggregated or 16 disaggregated) and on B200, B300, GB200, and GB300 (NVFP4, 8 GPUs).
DFlash2 block length 8, FP8 KV cache with 64-token pages, and up to 1,048,576 context tokens on every target.
KV-aware routing: SGLang publishes KV events and vLLM uses prediction-based routing. Disaggregated targets move KV between prefill and decode over NIXL, and vLLM targets add native host offload.
An AIPerf synthetic chat benchmark (8,192 input and 1,024 output tokens, streaming, one concurrency point per Job).
Reflection logo: Added the Reflection provider logo to the recipe catalog (#16677).
Getting Started
Deployment is Kubernetes-based (Dynamo Platform + DynamoGraphDeployment). Full steps — namespace, model-cache PVC, Hugging Face download job (target checkpoint plus the DFlash2 draft), DGD apply, and a /v1/chat/completions smoke test — are in the recipe README. The benchmark workflow is in perf/README.md. For gated Hugging Face repositories, add an HF_TOKEN secret reference to the download Job.
Known Issues / Limitations
Experimental snapshot build — not QA-gated; not for production.
The shared-model-cache PVC needs at least 2Ti on a ReadWriteMany storage class; set storageClassName in model-cache/model-cache.yaml before applying it.
Disaggregated targets need GPUDirect-capable RDMA devices on both roles and NIXL/UCX connectivity between them. A TCP fallback works without RDMA, but KV transfer then goes through host memory and the pod network.
vLLM disaggregated targets register the whole KV pool as one memory region. If the NIC rejects it (NIXL_ERR_BACKEND), lower --gpu-memory-utilization; the B300 and GB300 disaggregated profiles already ship at 0.5.
Every target requires the DFlash2 draft checkpoint in addition to the target checkpoint.
